name: Southern Ocean
genZNote: The Southern Ocean is the quiet one — no countries actually border it (Antarctica isn't a country), but it basically runs the planet's climate system from the back office.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Extent
bullets: Encircles Antarctica, generally defined as the waters south of 60°S latitude, though some definitions extend it further north to the Antarctic Convergence.
The most recently formally recognised of the major oceans — many older atlases folded it into the southern Pacific, Atlantic and Indian Oceans instead.
The only ocean that completely encircles the globe without hitting a landmass, at the latitude of the Drake Passage and beyond.

sections.heading: 🗺️ What Borders It
bullets: Antarctica is its only landmass border — Antarctica is a continent, not a sovereign country, governed under the Antarctic Treaty System rather than owned by any nation.
No country has a permanent population on its coastline; several countries (including India) operate seasonal scientific research stations on Antarctica.
The Drake Passage, between South America's Cape Horn and the Antarctic Peninsula, is its narrowest and most turbulent crossing point.

sections.heading: 🚢 Trade, Research & Strategic Importance
bullets: Carries essentially no commercial shipping trade — it's far too remote, cold and rough for regular commercial routes.
Its main human activity is scientific research: climate science, glaciology, and Antarctic marine biology.
The Antarctic Circumpolar Current, the world's largest ocean current by volume transported, flows uninterrupted around Antarctica and links the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian Oceans.
India operates Antarctic research stations (see the India Maritime profile) as part of its scientific presence here.

sections.heading: 🐧 Marine Ecology & Environmental Concerns
bullets: Extremely rich in krill — tiny crustaceans that form the base of a food web supporting whales, seals, penguins and seabirds.
Some of the most pristine, least human-disturbed marine ecosystems on Earth, though increasingly monitored for the effects of warming and sea-ice loss.
Antarctic sea-ice extent is one of the most closely watched indicators in global climate science.
Regulated commercial krill fishing exists under international agreements (CCAMLR) designed to prevent overexploitation of this foundational species.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Southern Ocean encircles Antarctica south of roughly 60°S and drives the Antarctic Circumpolar Current, the world's largest ocean current.
keyFacts: Encircles Antarctica; most recently recognised major ocean.
No country borders it directly — Antarctica is not a sovereign nation.
Antarctic Circumpolar Current links the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian Oceans.
Krill-based food web supports whales, seals and penguins.
commonConfusion: Don't list any country as "bordering" the Southern Ocean the way you would for other oceans — Antarctica has no sovereign owner.

highYieldFacts: Southern Ocean = waters around Antarctica, roughly south of 60°S.
Antarctic Circumpolar Current — largest ocean current by volume, flows uninterrupted around the globe.
Governed under the Antarctic Treaty System, not any single country.
commonTraps: Don't confuse the Antarctic Treaty System (governance of the continent) with CCAMLR (marine resource management).
mustRemember: Southern Ocean = around Antarctica; Antarctic Circumpolar Current; krill-based ecosystem; no sovereign coastal country.
